newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of England Inflation Report.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of England Inflation Report.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to the Bank of England's quarterly Inflation Report, in which the central bank said further moderate policy tightening was needed and sterling's rise should push RPIX well below 2.5 percent this year:
"Certainly not as market-friendly as we were expecting. The surprise is that they are still calling for another tightening of policy before seeing the effects of the last one."

"Last week's base rate increase has failed to eradicate the Bank's concerns over inflation in the medium term. Taxes will have to rise in the forthcoming mini-budget if a further near-term tightening in monetary policy is to be avoided."

"For me this is not so much of a surprise. Certainly it was the case that RPI-X would dip below its 2.5 percent target in the near term. But given the hotting up of domestic demand, the broader money supply and average earnings, it is not that surprising that the bank sees a need for moderate rate rises and says that it is more than likely that the 2.5 percent target will not be met at the end of next year."
"The Bank's stance looks a little bit tougher than some optimists might have hoped for, but it shows the Bank is going to do what is necessary.
"The market should be fairly comfortable with this report. It has priced in modest (rate) increases and without them it may begin to worry."
